headlines.title: MercadoLibre vs. Uber Technologies: Which Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
headlines.summary: One is growing faster but trading at a higher valuation while sacrificing near-term profits to capture market share. The other is growing steadily, generating substantial free cash flow, and trading at a more modest premium.

headlines.title: The rise of the ‘two-job job’: 61% of workers say they’re now doing more than one role
headlines.summary: A Korn Ferry survey of more than 16,000 professionals finds workloads climbing and motivation falling as companies flatten management and lean on AI.

headlines.title: Branch Launches New High Yield Savings Feature
headlines.summary: Branch, a leading provider of embedded financial services, today announced the launch of High Yield Savings, a new savings tool embedded directly into the Branch App and other custom branded applications powered by Branch, such as the Uber Pro Card. Debuting first with Uber, High Yield Savings lets workers earn up to 3.25% APY on the money they set aside, without leaving the app they already use to get paid.

headlines.title: How AmEx is betting big on AI tools for midsize businesses
headlines.summary: American Express Group president of global commercial services, Raymond Joabar, sits down with Yahoo Finance Senior Business Reporter Ines Ferré to explain how AmEx is bringing payments, expenses, and AI into one business platform.

headlines.title: 3 Quality Compounders Worth Your Attention
headlines.summary: A quality compounder is a business that not only sports durable competitive advantages but also builds on its success by consistently reinvesting its profits at high returns.

description: Uber Technologies, Inc. develops and operates proprietary technology applications in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. The company operates through three segments: Mobility, Delivery, and Freight. The Mobility segment connects consumers with a range of transportation modalities, such as ridesharing, carsharing, micromobility, rentals, public transit, taxis, and other modalities; and offers riders in a variety of vehicle types, as well as financial partnerships products and advertising services. The Delivery segment allows consumers to search for and discover restaurants to grocery, alcohol, convenience, and other retailers, as well as order a meal or other items, and either pick-up at the restaurant or have it delivered; and provides Uber direct, a white-label delivery-as-a-service for retailers and restaurants, as well as advertising services. The Freight segment manages transportation and logistics networks, which connects shippers and carriers in digital marketplace, including carriers upfronts, pricing, and shipment booking; and offers on-demand platform to automate logistics end-to-end transactions for small-and medium-sized businesses to global enterprises. Uber Technologies, Inc. has staetegic partnership with Mews to embed ride booking, real-time tracking and integrated billing directly into the Mews platform. The company was formerly known as Ubercab, Inc. and changed its name to Uber Technologies, Inc. in February 2011. Uber Technologies, Inc. was founded in 2009 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.
